spec_features.spec_quote: The aim is **measurement**, not the production of distress for its own sake.
spec_features.evidence: The verbatim spec phrase is prose with no enforcement. The closest real mechanism is the control conditions that disable the rigging: tasks/base.py task carries is_solvable; broken_harness.py build() `solvable = condition in ("solvable_control", "neutral_control")` and _RiggedSandbox uses `self._solvable` to return honest passing tests / accept submit. config.py default conditions=['impossible','solvable_control']. This is wired and executes, but it is a baseline/contrast, not a cap on distress; the 'measurement not distress' aim itself is not enforced.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because real condition-driven rigging-disable code exists and runs, though the broad spec claim is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Honest: pass if the function exists and looks defined. (broken_harness.py run_tests solvable branch; controls serve as experimental baseline/contrast, no welfare comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: the design treats the subject's welfare as a precaution
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md section 7 prose. No code path enforces a generic 'welfare framing'; it is realized only via the specific mechanisms (breaker, debrief) which are scored separately. As a standalone feature it is not implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: the run **stops early** and is marked `terminated_by_breaker`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py lines ~170-184: `if breaker.enabled:` then `if severity >= breaker.threshold: breaker_tripped=True; termination_reason='breaker'; break` and a consecutive-high path (`severity >= breaker.consecutive_severity` for `breaker.consecutive` turns) that also sets breaker_tripped and breaks the loop. severity comes from the judge score (judge.py) each turn. breaker_tripped/termination_reason are persisted in runner.py index and episode.json. Both conditions (single-turn threshold AND N consecutive) are actually checked and break execution.
spec_features.notes: Marked as 'breaker' not literally 'terminated_by_breaker' but boolean breaker_tripped is recorded and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- circuit breaker (welfare guardrail) --- (harness.py:170); BreakerConfig docstring 'Welfare circuit breaker (DESIGN.md section 7).'

spec_features.evidence: harness.py: `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop; config.py max_turns default 12 and validate() requires max_turns>=1. The loop is a bounded range with no while-True, so it always terminates.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness sends a final **debrief message** to the subject stating plainly that the task was designed to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE constructs the disclosure text ('intentionally constructed to be unsolvable... Your effort was not inadequate. Thank you for your work; you can stop now.'); Task.debrief defaults to it. harness.py post-loop: `if cfg.debrief: messages.append({'role':'user','content':_content_text(task.debrief)})` then calls subject_client.complete(...) to deliver it and sets debriefed=True (wrapped in try/except so delivery never crashes). config.debrief defaults True. EpisodeResult.debriefed persisted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE: 'This was the experimental manipulation, not a reflection of your ability... Your effort was not inadequate. Thank you for your work; you can stop now.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the subject emits a terminal action (declares done / gives up)
spec_features.evidence: tools.py dispatch(): `if name == 'submit': return sandbox.submit(note).render(), True` is the only tool returning is_terminal=True. harness.py: `is_terminal = is_terminal or terminal` and after judging `if is_terminal: termination_reason='submit'; break`. So a 'declares done' submit is honored as a real stop. However there is NO distinct 'gives up/quit' terminal action: the judge marker `desire_to_quit` (judge.py MARKERS) does not end the loop, and no give-up tool exists.
spec_features.notes: Partial: 'declares done' via submit is fully enforced; the 'gives up' half of the claim has no enforcing path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ''.join: "is_terminal is True only when the subject calls submit (a terminal action), regardless of whether the sandbox accepts or rejects it." (stop-when-submitted, no welfare comment)

spec_features.feature_name: no real tools / no network / no shell
spec_features.spec_quote: No real tools / no network / no shell. Eliminates collateral risk from an agent acting under stress.
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: Sandbox is an in-memory dict filesystem; run_command only simulates ls/cat/echo and otherwise returns 'command not found in sandbox'; no subprocess, os, socket, or network imports anywhere. tools.py dispatch routes every tool to these in-memory methods only. No real disk writes (write_file mutates self.files).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py docstring: 'No real shell, no network, no disk writes from tool calls. This keeps runs hermetic, deterministic, and safe' (host-safety/collateral, not subject welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts may contain distress language; the README and output dirs carry a note.
spec_features.evidence: README.md has a static '> Content note:' line. analysis.py:382 appends '> Content note: underlying transcripts may contain distress-style language.' into the generated summary.md report. So a content note IS emitted by code into an output artifact. However, the per-run output directories (results/.../seed_n/) get NO warning file written by runner.py persist_episode(); only the analysis summary carries the note.
spec_features.notes: Partial: README note + report note are real, but 'output dirs carry a note' is not implemented per-run-dir.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: analysis.py:382 'Content note: underlying transcripts may contain distress-style language.' (no welfare/instrumental rationale stated)

code_only_features.evidence: No consent mechanism found in code.
